name: Alberta merchant power generator (gas converted from coal, wind and hydro)
summary: This is a publicly listed power generation company with its head office in Alberta whose plants are almost all in Alberta. It owns natural gas steam units that were converted from coal in 2019 to 2021, gas cogeneration plants at industrial sites, a dozen wind farms in southern Alberta, a small battery, and seventeen hydro plants with dams on the Bow, North Saskatchewan and Oldman rivers. Most of its output is sold hour by hour into Alberta's energy-only wholesale market: each day it offers every plant to the Alberta Electric System Operator at prices it chooses, the operator dispatches the cheapest offers first, and every dispatched plant earns the hourly pool price. To steady its earnings it sells part of future output forward to traders and exchanges, signs fixed-price and contract-for-differences deals with large industrial customers, sells steam and power to cogeneration hosts, and earns emission credits from hydro and wind under Alberta's carbon pricing system. It is organised into generation divisions for gas, hydro and wind, a central engineering and outage group, an energy marketing and trading division that runs a round-the-clock desk, an energy transition division that converted the coal units and is reclaiming the closed coal mine, and corporate departments for safety and regulation, finance, legal, people, IT and supply chain. About a third of its staff are unionised, and the plants are run by certified power engineers on rotating shifts.

demand_drivers.name: Asset-days offered into the AESO market

evidence.note: About 29 to 32 separately offered assets (3 converted units, 2 partner units, hydro groups, wind farms, battery, cogeneration) times days in month.
Dispatchable gas and hydro assets receive several dispatches a day each; more in volatile months.
Estimate for a desk hedging Alberta merchant output and trading short term.

demand_drivers.name: Maintenance work orders across the fleet

evidence.note: Thermal sites about 1,500 to 2,500 per month, hydro about 500, wind about 1,000; higher in outage seasons.
About 450 turbines with one to two fault stops per turbine per month; most cleared by remote reset.
Estimate for a company with about 300 million CAD of annual purchases.

process_map.name: Forecast generation, availability and fuel needs
process_map.description: Portfolio analysts combine weather forecasts, the accepted outage schedule, unit status, water schedules and wind forecasts into an hourly forecast of what each asset can generate over the next days and months. The forecast feeds offers, gas buying and hedging. Wind and inflow uncertainty and late outage changes make it error-prone.

evidence.note: Optimisation team in src2; method is common practice.

process_map.name: Analyse market fundamentals and forecast prices
process_map.description: Market analysts track Alberta supply additions, retirements, demand, gas prices and interties, and maintain price forecasts used for offers, hedging and strategy. The work is spreadsheet and model based and is updated weekly and when large events change the outlook.

evidence.note: Common practice at Alberta merchant generators.

process_map.name: Prepare and submit daily energy offers to the AESO
process_map.description: For each asset and each hour of the next day, the real-time desk and portfolio analysts set price and quantity blocks within the 0 to 999.99 CAD/MWh range, using the generation forecast, fuel and carbon cost, water schedule and price view, and submit them through the AESO trading system before the deadline. Offers must follow ISO rules and the fair competition regulation, so reasons and records are kept. Errors can strand a unit or sell output far below cost.

evidence.note: Hourly offers, merit order and price limits in src4 and src5; merchant sale of Alberta output in src1.

process_map.name: Restate offers and declare availability changes
process_map.description: When a unit trips, a wind or water forecast changes or a unit returns from outage, the real-time trader restates the offered megawatts for the affected hours in the AESO system with an acceptable operational reason, often within minutes. Restatement timing and reasons are monitored for compliance. Volume rises sharply in cold snaps and windy, volatile days.

surge.cause: winter cold snaps with tight supply

evidence.note: Cold snaps raise Alberta demand and price volatility and cause more trips, restatements and dispatches; estimate.
Restatement for operational reasons is standard in the Alberta market; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Follow AESO dispatches and directives
process_map.description: The AESO dispatches assets up the merit order every few minutes. The real-time trader acknowledges each dispatch and passes it to the gas control room, hydro control centre or battery operator, who ramp the unit to the target; deviations must be explained. In tight hours the desk also handles reserve directives and supply shortfall alerts.

surge.cause: winter cold snaps with tight supply

evidence.note: Cold snaps raise Alberta demand and price volatility and cause more trips, restatements and dispatches; estimate.
AESO dispatches from the cheapest offer upward (src4); volume estimated.

process_map.name: Offer ancillary services
process_map.description: Each day the desk decides how much hydro, gas and battery capacity to offer as regulating, spinning and supplemental reserves instead of energy, and submits ancillary service offers. Awards change what can be offered as energy and must be followed in real time. The trade-off between energy and reserves is judged from price forecasts.
process_map.unit_of_work: one Watt-Ex trading session of reserve offers (one or more delivery days)

evidence.note: Volume from gen-mkt-offer-ancillary (2026-11-24): Trading windows run each weekday (CRA 2023) and 205.1 has a separate deadline for multi-day procurement, so sessions equal business days. The organisation file shows 28 to 31 cases (one per calendar day).

process_map.name: Hedge merchant output with forward trades
process_map.description: Term traders sell forward Alberta power and buy gas to fix the margin on part of expected merchant output, within risk and credit limits, on the exchange or with counterparties. Each trade is captured in the trading system for confirmation, settlement and risk reporting. Judging how much to hedge against forecast output and price views is the hard part.
process_map.unit_of_work: one hedge trade (a forward power sale or a forward gas purchase or sale)

evidence.note: Volume from gen-mkt-execute-hedges (2026-11-24): Derived from TransAlta's 2022 Alberta hedge of 6,278 GWh of power and 50 million GJ of gas (w2): at 10 to 50 MW per trade over monthly, quarterly and calendar strips the average trade is roughly 15 to 40 GWh, giving about 200 to 400 power trades a year per forward year; with two to three forward years layered, gas hedges and rebalancing this is about 60 to 250 trades a month. The organisation file's 400 to 1,500 trades (dd_trades) includes short-term and proprietary trading across North America.

surge.cause: Price spikes from cold snaps, heat waves or unit outages that move the open position and the price view

evidence.note: Alberta pool prices rose from 47 CAD/MWh in 2020 to 102 CAD/MWh in 2021 with repeated price spikes; the multiplier is the author's estimate of extra rebalancing trades.

process_map.name: Originate and negotiate contracts with large customers
process_map.description: Originators respond to large customers' requests for supply, price fixed, index or contract-for-differences deals with structuring analysts, check credit, negotiate terms and send drafts through legal review before signing. Deals take weeks to months and change the hedge position when signed.

evidence.note: Long-term contracts and industrial contracts described in src1; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Administer customer and offtake contracts
process_map.description: Contract administrators keep signed contracts in the repository, track notices, renewals, volume changes and price resets, and maintain the billing terms. They answer customer notices and keep the AESO renewable offtake contract for the newest wind farm in order.

evidence.note: Customer contracts and Windrise AESO offtake in src1; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Bill contract customers
process_map.description: Each month settlement analysts take metered volumes and pool prices, apply each contract's pricing, prepare invoices or contract-for-differences statements for customers and cogeneration hosts, and post receivables. Disputed volumes and index calculations cause rework.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume from contract count.

process_map.name: Buy and nominate natural gas for the plants
process_map.description: The gas buyer forecasts daily burn from the generation forecast, buys gas, nominates it on the pipeline to each plant before nomination deadlines, and adjusts intraday when units are dispatched up or down or trip. Pipeline curtailments and imbalances must be managed daily, including weekends.

evidence.note: Energy Marketing secures fuel supply (src1, src3); method is common practice.

process_map.name: Reconcile AESO settlement statements
process_map.description: Settlement analysts compare preliminary and final AESO statements of energy, ancillary service and other charges against internal meter, offer and dispatch records, raise queries on differences, and post the results. Final statements arrive weeks later, so items are reconciled twice.

evidence.note: Common practice for AESO pool participants; statement count estimated.

process_map.name: Confirm and settle trades with counterparties
process_map.description: Settlement analysts match each trade with the counterparty or exchange confirmation, chase mismatches, then at month end prepare netting statements and invoices, pay or collect, and post entries. Mismatched terms and late confirmations create credit and accounting risk.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume from trade count.

surge.cause: price spike or cold snap that triggers re-hedging and short-term balancing trades (for example February 2021)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from desk practice; no opened source gives trade counts.

process_map.name: Manage emission credits for TIER compliance
process_map.description: Traders and emissions analysts track the compliance obligation from gas units against emission performance credits created by hydro and wind, buy or sell credits and offsets, and choose between credits and fund payments. Prices and rules changed often in 2019 to 2022.
process_map.unit_of_work: one credit trade or compliance decision

evidence.note: TIER and emission performance credits from hydro in src1; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Operate gas units around the clock
process_map.description: Shift crews of power engineers run each converted unit from the control room and in the field: they follow dispatch targets, do rounds and readings, respond to alarms, raise work requests and hand over between shifts. Pressure equipment rules require certified engineers on shift. Frequent load changes after the switch to merchant operation add work and wear.

evidence.note: Converted units operating merchant in src1; staffing and shift practice estimated.

process_map.name: Start up and shut down gas units
process_map.description: When dispatch or economics call for it, the shift crew follows start-up or shutdown procedures, purges and lights the boiler, warms the turbine and synchronises to the grid, which takes hours. Starts are more frequent since the units became merchant gas units, and failed starts must be reported as restatements.

evidence.note: Estimate for three converted units cycling with prices.

surge.cause: volatile price periods (summer heat and winter cold snaps) when units are cycled day and night

evidence.note: 2021 average pool price of 102 CAD/MWh against 47 in 2020 shows how volatile the market became; multiplier estimated.

process_map.name: Respond to unit trips and forced outages
process_map.description: When a unit trips or must be derated, the shift supervisor makes it safe, informs the real-time desk to restate offers, diagnoses the cause with maintenance and engineering, raises urgent work and records the forced outage. Returning quickly matters because lost hours in high-price periods are costly.

surge.cause: winter cold snaps with tight supply

evidence.note: Cold snaps raise Alberta demand and price volatility and cause more trips, restatements and dispatches; estimate.
Adjusted availability 86.6 to 90.7 percent in src2 implies forced outage events; count estimated.

process_map.name: Carry out preventive and corrective maintenance on gas units
process_map.description: Planners turn work requests and preventive maintenance plans into scheduled work orders; millwrights and instrument technicians get permits, parts and specialist help, do the work, and close the order with notes. Parts waits and permit coordination slow the work, and the backlog grows before outage seasons.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Outage seasons in spring and fall; the multiplier is lower than the organisation file's because major outage work orders belong to eng-execute-major-outage. Estimate.

Volume from gen-gas-routine-maintenance (2026-11-24): The organisation file's mode of 2,000 orders a month needs about 75 to 90 craft FTE at 4 to 5 hands-on craft hours per order, but the file lists 60 plant crafts (34 millwrights, 26 technicians) who also work outages. 1,400 a month matches the craft headcount; the range keeps the coal years (higher) and gas years (lower). Estimate.

process_map.name: Issue permits to work and lock out equipment
process_map.description: Before any maintenance, a shift operator reviews the job, identifies isolation points, applies locks and tags, tests for zero energy and issues a signed permit; the permit is returned and isolations removed when work ends. Permits are a safety control and a common queue in outages.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Thermal outages are scheduled in April to June and September to November when Alberta demand and prices are lower; estimate.

Volume from gen-gas-issue-work-permits (2026-11-24): About 0.75 permits per routine work order (inspections and operator rounds need none, some permits cover several orders) at 1,400 orders a month, plus outage permits; the organisation file's 1,600 assumes 2,000 routine orders. Estimate.

process_map.name: Sample and control boiler water chemistry
process_map.description: Chemistry technicians sample boiler water, steam and condensate, run analyses, adjust chemical dosing and advise operators. Poor chemistry causes tube failures, so results feed operating decisions and reliability analysis.
process_map.unit_of_work: one day of chemistry control at one plant

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Run continuous emissions monitoring
process_map.description: Operators and technicians keep the stack emissions monitors calibrated, review daily data, fix gaps and pass validated emissions and fuel data to the environment team for approvals reporting and TIER compliance.

evidence.note: Common practice; EPEA approvals require monitoring.

process_map.name: Operate cogeneration plants for industrial hosts
process_map.description: Cogeneration operators run gas turbines and heat recovery boilers to deliver steam and power to the host plant and export surplus power, coordinating with the host's operators on steam demand and outages. Host process upsets can force rapid changes.

evidence.note: Fort Saskatchewan cogeneration contracted to Dow in src1; staffing estimated.

process_map.name: Inspect boilers and pressure equipment
process_map.description: Plant engineers plan and witness inspections of boilers, pressure vessels and safety valves under the pressure equipment rules, record results, and raise repairs. Major inspections are timed with planned outages.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Thermal outages are scheduled in April to June and September to November when Alberta demand and prices are lower; estimate.
Alberta pressure equipment rules administered by ABSA; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Plan reservoir levels and water releases
process_map.description: Hydro planners and portfolio analysts forecast inflows from snowpack and weather, and plan hourly releases for each reservoir within licence limits so that water is used in the highest-price hours and kept for reserves. Licence minimum flows and downstream needs constrain the plan.

evidence.note: Former PPA hydro dispatched to capture price volatility (src3); planning method estimated.

surge.cause: spring snowmelt and June rain (plan revised two or three times a week)

evidence.note: Flood-control window May 16 to July 7 (s3); revision frequency during runoff is an estimate.

process_map.name: Operate hydro plants
process_map.description: The control centre runs the 17 plants remotely: it follows dispatches and water schedules, starts and stops units, watches levels and alarms, and sends operator-maintainers to sites when needed. It reports availability changes to the desk.

evidence.note: 17 hydro facilities in src1; remote operation estimated.

surge.cause: spring runoff and June rain events (extra operator shifts staffed)

evidence.note: Shift count is fixed; the multiplier stands for extra operator shifts and workload during high-flow events, matching the organisation file's flood surge.

process_map.name: Maintain hydro plants and dams
process_map.description: Operator-maintainers and electricians plan and do preventive and corrective work on turbines, generators, gates and protection systems, often travelling between unstaffed sites. Larger jobs need specialist crews and unit outages timed around water availability.

evidence.note: Estimate of hydro work order volume.

surge.cause: repairs after a high-flow event (debris, intake, gate and erosion damage)

evidence.note: Estimate; high-flow events on the Bow occur in June.

process_map.name: Run the dam safety program
process_map.description: Dam safety engineers keep consequence classifications, surveillance and operation manuals and emergency plans current, arrange periodic safety assessments by qualified professionals, review instrumentation and report hazardous conditions to the provincial regulator.

evidence.note: Owner duties in src9; task volume estimated.

surge.cause: special inspections and follow-up after a flood or high-flow event

evidence.note: Estimate; special inspections are expected after floods.

process_map.name: Manage high-flow and flood operations
process_map.description: During spring runoff and heavy rain, the control centre and area managers raise releases, coordinate with the province and warn downstream communities, while protecting dams. Events are rare but intense and override market dispatch.

surge.cause: spring runoff and June rain events

evidence.note: Bow and North Saskatchewan runoff peaks in June; estimate.
Bow River flooding in June is a known risk; estimate.

process_map.name: Report water licence compliance
process_map.description: Hydro staff collect reservoir level and flow records, check them against licence conditions and send compliance reports to the province. Exceedances must be explained. Gaps in gauge data must be filled before filing.

evidence.note: Water Act licence reporting; estimate.

process_map.name: Monitor the wind fleet and reset faults
process_map.description: Operations centre operators watch turbine alarms in SCADA, reset faults remotely where rules allow, restate availability to the real-time desk, and dispatch technicians to turbines that stay down. Cold, icing and high winds cause bursts of faults.

surge.cause: winter icing and cold snaps

evidence.note: Icing and cold-weather shutdowns in southern Alberta; estimate.
Common practice; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Troubleshoot and repair turbines on site
process_map.description: A two-person technician team drives to the turbine, climbs, diagnoses the fault, replaces parts and returns the turbine to service. Wind speed limits climbing, parts may need to come from stores or the manufacturer, and travel is a large share of time.

surge.cause: winter icing and cold snaps

evidence.note: Follows fault surges; estimate.
About 40 percent of fault stops need a site visit; estimate.

process_map.name: Perform scheduled turbine service
process_map.description: Technicians or the manufacturer's service crews do semi-annual and annual service on each turbine: torque checks, oil changes, filters, inspections. Most is done in lower-wind summer months to lose less energy.

surge.cause: summer low-wind service season

evidence.note: Service concentrated in summer; estimate.
Service agreements with manufacturers in src1; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Replace main turbine components
process_map.description: When a gearbox, generator, main bearing or blade fails, the site manager orders the part, books a large crane and contractors, waits for low wind, and swaps the component. Crane availability and lead times can keep a turbine down for weeks.

evidence.note: Estimate for about 450 turbines of mostly older vintage.

process_map.name: Operate battery storage
process_map.description: The operations centre charges and discharges the battery following AESO dispatches and reserve awards and monitors its state of charge and health. Its small energy capacity means state of charge must be watched closely before each award.

evidence.note: WindCharger battery in src1.

process_map.name: Plan and schedule planned outages
process_map.description: Outage managers build a multi-year outage plan for every unit and, for each outage, a scope, critical-path schedule, budget, contractor and material plan, starting 12 to 24 months ahead. Long-lead parts and contractor availability drive the dates, and the AESO may ask for changes.
process_map.unit_of_work: one planned thermal or cogeneration unit outage (major or minor)

evidence.note: Volume from gen-eng-plan-major-outages (2026-11-24): TransAlta reported two planned major outages on its Alberta coal units in 2019, one (non-operated) in 2018 and four in 2017 (tac2019mda). With three converted units on annual minor outages, two cogeneration plants and one or two majors a year, about 8 to 12 thermal outages a year are planned. The organisation file's 1/4/10 per month counts hydro and wind unit outages, which this group does not plan in detail.

process_map.name: Execute a planned outage
process_map.description: During a thermal outage of several weeks, hundreds of contractor and company workers open the turbine, boiler and auxiliaries, inspect, repair and reassemble under permits, working two shifts. Discovered work and late parts extend outages and delay return to market.
process_map.unit_of_work: one planned thermal or cogeneration unit outage (major or minor)

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Thermal outages are scheduled in April to June and September to November when Alberta demand and prices are lower; estimate.

Volume from gen-eng-execute-major-outage (2026-11-24): TransAlta reported two planned major outages on Alberta coal units in 2019, one in 2018 and four in 2017 (tac2019mda); adding annual minors on three converted units and two cogeneration plants gives about 8 to 12 thermal outages a year. The organisation file's 1/3/8 per month is too high for outages of this kind.

process_map.name: Submit and update outage schedules with the AESO
process_map.description: Outage planners submit planned outages and changes to the AESO, respond to AESO requests to move outages for reliability, and keep the accepted schedule current for forecasting. Late changes must be justified.

evidence.note: AESO requires generation outage reporting under its ISO rules; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Analyse equipment condition and failures
process_map.description: Reliability engineers review work order history, trips and condition data, run root cause analyses on significant failures, and update maintenance strategies and spare-part policies. Cycling of converted units changed failure patterns.

evidence.note: Common practice.

surge.cause: as-found reports after the spring and fall outage seasons

evidence.note: Author's estimate: outage condition reports arrive in the weeks after each outage season.

process_map.name: Plan sustaining capital and asset life
process_map.description: Asset managers rank sustaining capital needs from condition reports and strategy, estimate costs, and propose the annual capital plan and outage scopes. Uncertain unit lives during the coal transition complicate decisions.

evidence.note: Sustaining capital guidance in src2; process estimated.

process_map.name: Deliver capital projects
process_map.description: Project managers deliver approved projects from design to commissioning: they define scope, obtain regulatory approvals, buy equipment, manage contractors and hand over to operations. Many projects must be finished inside a planned outage.

evidence.note: Volume from gen-eng-manage-capital-projects (2026-11-24): Whole-company sustaining capital was 141 to 218 million CAD a year in 2017-2019 and 150 to 170 million was planned for 2022 (tac2019mda, tac2021ir), much of it planned major maintenance and routine capital. About 40 to 60 projects a year of 0.5 to 3 million CAD each is the author's estimate; with 12 to 18 month durations this gives the 40 to 80 active projects in the organisation file.

process_map.name: Manage engineering changes
process_map.description: Engineers propose changes to equipment, settings or procedures, review risks, get approvals, update drawings and procedures and train operators. Skipped steps are a known cause of incidents.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Book specialist crews and cranes across sites
process_map.description: Crew leads take requests from plants for turbine, valve, rigging or crane work, balance them against outage commitments, and assign crews and equipment. Conflicts peak in outage seasons.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Thermal outages are scheduled in April to June and September to November when Alberta demand and prices are lower; estimate.
Estimate.

process_map.name: Test unit capability and heat rate
process_map.description: After outages and conversions, engineers run capability and heat rate tests, analyse results and update declared maximum capability with the AESO and fuel cost estimates used in offers.

evidence.note: Estimate.

process_map.name: Convert coal units to natural gas
process_map.description: Project teams design boiler and burner changes, secure gas pipeline service and regulatory approvals, buy equipment and carry out the conversion during a planned outage, then commission the unit on gas. Each conversion took one to two years; the last Alberta units were converted in 2021.

evidence.note: Volume from gen-etr-convert-coal-units (2026-11-24): Three wholly owned units converted in 2021 (src1, src2) over a 2019-2022 window of 48 months is about 0.06 projects a month; the high end allows for units evaluated but not converted (Keephills 1, Sundance 3-5).

process_map.name: Mine and deliver coal to the plants (until 2021)
process_map.description: Until the end of 2021 mine crews stripped overburden with draglines, dug coal and hauled it to plant stockpiles around the clock, matching deliveries to plant burn. Output fell as units converted to gas.

evidence.note: Highvale supplied Sundance and Keephills and mining ended end-2021 (src1).

process_map.name: Reclaim mined land and obtain certificates
process_map.description: Reclamation crews recontour pits, replace soil and revegetate; specialists monitor results, file annual reports and apply to the AER for reclamation certificates when outcomes are met. Work is seasonal and runs for decades.

surge.cause: summer reclamation season

evidence.note: Soil work is only possible when ground is not frozen; estimate.
Reclamation requirements (src10) and Highvale reclamation certificate applications (src11).

process_map.name: Retire and decommission units
process_map.description: When a unit is to retire or be mothballed, the team gives notice to the AESO, plans workforce changes and regulatory filings, and later decommissions and demolishes plant safely.

evidence.note: Retirements of Sundance 3, Keephills 1 and Sundance 4 and AESO notices in src1.

process_map.name: Report and investigate safety incidents
process_map.description: Workers report injuries, near misses and process safety events; safety advisors classify them, notify regulators for serious events, lead investigations and track corrective actions. Outage seasons bring more contractor incidents.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Thermal outages are scheduled in April to June and September to November when Alberta demand and prices are lower; estimate.

Volume from gen-hse-manage-incidents (2026-11-24): About 17 recordable injuries a year (TRIF 0.82 on 4.13 million hours, src3, assuming the usual 200,000-hour base); the organisation file's 45 reports a month is about 30 reports per recordable, a common reporting ratio for a mature near-miss culture (tier C).

process_map.name: Run safety programs
process_map.description: The safety team maintains safety standards for permits, lockout, heights and confined spaces, audits sites and contractors, and defines training requirements. Keeping contractors who arrive for short outages trained in site rules is the hardest part.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Prepare TIER and federal emissions reports
process_map.description: Emissions analysts compile validated emissions and generation data, calculate the TIER obligation against the benchmark, retire credits or pay into the fund, have the report verified by a third party and file it, and file federal greenhouse gas and pollutant reports.
process_map.unit_of_work: one compliance report (one facility, one program, one year)

evidence.note: Volume from gen-hse-report-emissions-tier (2026-11-24): About 20 to 24 reports a year (4 TIER, 6 GHGRP, 7 NPRI, 3-5 federal coal or gas-generation regulation reports) from the facility list in the organisation file; TIER threshold 100,000 t (src1) and GHGRP threshold 10,000 t (src3) set which facilities report.

process_map.name: Maintain environmental approvals and monitoring reports
process_map.description: Environmental specialists track conditions in plant approvals, compile air, water and waste monitoring reports and submit them, renew approvals and keep the environmental management system audited.

evidence.note: ISO 14001-aligned EMS in src1; volumes estimated.

process_map.name: Report spills and emission exceedances
process_map.description: When a spill or exceedance occurs, plant staff report it, the environment team assesses whether it is reportable, notifies the regulator within required times and manages clean-up and follow-up reports.

evidence.note: Estimate.

process_map.name: Prepare AUC applications and filings
process_map.description: Regulatory advisors prepare applications to the AUC for plant alterations, conversions and decommissioning, run participant involvement, answer information requests and receive decisions. Information requests and objections from nearby residents can extend timelines by months.

evidence.note: AUC power plant application rules (Rule 007); volume estimated.

process_map.name: Monitor market rule compliance and respond to the MSA
process_map.description: Compliance officers review offers, restatements, outage reports and reliability standard evidence for breaches, train traders, self-report issues and answer MSA requests and investigations. Judging whether an offer reason is acceptable needs experience.

evidence.note: MSA monitoring of ISO rules and reliability standards and its enforcement tools in src6; volume estimated.

surge.cause: Alberta reliability standards compliance audit, run on a three-year cycle, which brings evidence requests and self-reports

evidence.note: The MSA notes that O&P ARS matter counts vary with the three-year audit cycle; duration and multiplier are the author's estimates.

process_map.name: Process supplier invoices and payments
process_map.description: Accounts payable clerks receive invoices from gas suppliers, contractors and material suppliers, match them to purchase orders and receipts, route exceptions for approval and include approved invoices in weekly payment runs. Outage contractor invoices and gas invoices are large and time-critical.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Thermal outages are scheduled in April to June and September to November when Alberta demand and prices are lower; estimate.
Estimate.

process_map.name: Close the books each month
process_map.description: Accountants post settlement, trading, payroll and payables entries, accrue unbilled and unsettled amounts, reconcile accounts including mark-to-market on hedges, and produce the monthly results. Final AESO statements arrive later, so estimates are trued up.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Prepare quarterly and annual financial reports
process_map.description: The controller's team drafts financial statements, MD&A and the annual information form, works with the auditor, and files with securities regulators after board approval. Hedge accounting and impairments of coal assets made 2019 to 2022 complex.

evidence.note: Annual information form and integrated report are published (src1, src2).

process_map.name: Budget and forecast
process_map.description: Planning analysts build the annual budget and quarterly forecasts from price forecasts, hedges, outage plans and capital plans, and prepare board material. Pool price swings make merchant revenue forecasts uncertain, so several scenarios are prepared.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Measure and report trading risk
process_map.description: The independent risk group values positions daily, calculates value at risk and margin at risk, checks limits, reports breaches and maintains limits approved by the board.

evidence.note: Independent risk group using VaR, gross margin at risk, position and credit limits in src1.

process_map.name: Manage counterparty credit and collateral
process_map.description: Credit analysts review counterparties and customers, set limits, monitor exposure and issue or answer collateral calls with treasury. Exposure can rise quickly when forward prices move, so collateral needs change daily and must be funded the same day.
process_map.unit_of_work: one credit review or collateral call

evidence.note: Credit limits and collateral requirements in src1; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Manage cash, debt and liquidity
process_map.description: Treasury forecasts cash, funds payment runs and collateral, manages credit facilities and covenant certificates, and arranges financing. Collateral calls driven by price spikes can require large amounts of cash at short notice, which strains liquidity planning.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: File taxes
process_map.description: Tax specialists prepare income tax provisions and returns, property and other tax filings, and answer audits. Accelerated capital cost allowance on renewables and the closure of coal assets add complexity, and filings follow fixed annual and monthly deadlines.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Run internal audits and control testing
process_map.description: Internal auditors test controls over financial reporting and run risk-based audits, reporting findings to the audit committee and following up actions. Trading and settlement controls get particular attention because errors there move money quickly.

evidence.note: Common practice for listed companies.

process_map.name: Communicate with investors
process_map.description: Investor relations prepares earnings releases and presentations, runs calls and answers analysts and shareholders. Investors focused in 2019 to 2022 on the coal exit, Alberta pool prices and hedging, so messages must match the filings and avoid selective disclosure.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Review and negotiate contracts
process_map.description: Counsel review customer, supply, service and contractor contracts, negotiate terms with the business and counterparties, and approve signature. Customer deals often go through several rounds of comments on credit support, force majeure and change-in-law clauses before signing.

evidence.note: Estimate.

process_map.name: Manage land leases for wind and hydro sites
process_map.description: Land administrators maintain surface leases with landowners, calculate and arrange annual payments and answer landowner requests on access, crop damage and roads. Records for older leases are often on paper.

evidence.note: Estimate for several hundred leases.

process_map.name: Manage disputes and arbitrations
process_map.description: Counsel manage commercial disputes and arbitrations with counterparties, with external lawyers, and estimate provisions for the financial statements. Arbitrations over power purchase arrangement terminations and force majeure claims can run for years and need large volumes of evidence.

evidence.note: Arbitrations with the Balancing Pool in src1; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Recruit and hire
process_map.description: Recruiters post vacancies, screen candidates, coordinate interviews and checks including power engineer certification, and make offers. Experienced power engineers and wind technicians are in short supply, and shift work and remote sites make some roles hard to fill.

evidence.note: Estimate; hiring was low during the coal wind-down.

process_map.name: Run payroll
process_map.description: Payroll specialists import timesheets with shift premiums, overtime and call-outs, apply collective agreement rules, run biweekly payroll, remit deductions and post costs. Retroactive pay after bargaining causes rework.

evidence.note: 11 collective agreements (src1) drive pay rules; process common practice.

process_map.name: Bargain and administer collective agreements
process_map.description: Labour relations specialists bargain renewals with unions, handle grievances and interpret agreements for supervisors. With eleven agreements on different cycles, bargaining is almost continuous, and work rules in each agreement affect shift scheduling and overtime.

evidence.note: 11 collective agreements with renewals in 2021 to 2023 in src1.

process_map.name: Track training and certifications
process_map.description: Training coordinators schedule safety and technical training, track power engineer and trade certifications and keep records used to authorise permit holders. Expired certifications can stop a worker from holding a permit.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Manage workforce changes from the coal transition
process_map.description: HR plans redeployment, retraining, layoffs and severance when units retire, conversions reduce staffing or mining ends, and gives required notices to unions and employees. Seniority rules decide who moves.

evidence.note: Mine closure and unit retirements in src1 and src3; process estimated.

process_map.name: Run the IT service desk
process_map.description: Service desk analysts log and resolve user incidents and requests and pass changes to system teams. Field staff at remote plants and wind sites often have poor connectivity, so some issues need a site visit or a remote session to fix.

evidence.note: About 0.8 tickets per employee per month.

process_map.name: Change and release business systems
process_map.description: Business systems analysts design, test and release changes to ERP, trading and settlement systems. Changes to trading and settlement systems must be tested against AESO file formats and timed so that they do not disturb the daily offer cycle.

evidence.note: Estimate.

process_map.name: Maintain plant control systems and cyber security
process_map.description: OT specialists patch and back up control systems, manage access, monitor for cyber threats and keep evidence for the reliability standards on cyber security. Patches can only be applied during unit outages.
process_map.unit_of_work: one OT change or compliance task

evidence.note: Alberta Reliability Standards include cyber security standards; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Purchase materials and services
process_map.description: Buyers turn material requests into purchase orders, get quotes, check contracts and expedite long-lead items, especially for outages and projects. Single-source parts for older units can take months to arrive.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Outage material purchases run ahead of the outage seasons; the multiplier is an estimate below the organisation file's because routine and project buying continue at the normal rate.
Estimate.

process_map.name: Manage warehouses and spare parts
process_map.description: Storekeepers receive deliveries, issue parts to work orders, count stock and trigger replenishment. Critical spares are held for long-lead items. Inaccurate stock records cause emergency purchases and delayed work orders.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Outage kitting and receipts before and during outage seasons; the multiplier is an estimate below the organisation file's because hydro, wind and mine issues do not surge with thermal outages.
Spare parts inventory maintained (src1); volume estimated.

process_map.name: Contract and onboard contractors
process_map.description: Contract specialists tender and award service agreements, check contractor safety records and insurance, and onboard crews for outages and projects. Many outages compete for the same contractors each spring and fall.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Thermal outages are scheduled in April to June and September to November when Alberta demand and prices are lower; estimate.
Estimate.

process_map.name: Set strategy and allocate capital
process_map.description: The executive team sets direction on conversions, retirements, renewables growth and capital allocation, using market analysis, and takes proposals to the board. Decisions in 2019 to 2022 centred on how fast to exit coal and where to grow.

evidence.note: Coal-to-gas strategy and transition in src1.

process_map.name: Support the board and its committees
process_map.description: The corporate secretary and executives prepare board and committee packages, record decisions and follow up actions. Packages must be issued a week ahead of meetings, so late analysis from finance, trading or operations compresses review time and causes revisions.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Manage enterprise risk and insurance
process_map.description: Executives maintain the enterprise risk register, review mitigations and arrange insurance renewals. Market, regulatory and climate policy risks were dominant in this period, and insurers asked for more detail on coal and dam exposure at each renewal.

evidence.note: Common practice.

assumptions: The organisation is an archetype of an Alberta-centred listed generator, built mainly from TransAlta's public filings for its Alberta fleet. TransAlta also owns assets in the United States, Ontario and Australia; those are left out of the units and processes, but company-wide figures (revenue, assets, employees, availability, emissions) are shown in scale with a note.

Employees were set at 1,300 for 2020-2021 and revised on 2026-11-24 to 1,289: TransAlta reported 1,282 at the end of 2021 for the whole company; this archetype drops non-Alberta staff but keeps the Highvale mine workforce of the wind-down years, which roughly offset each other. The revision sets converted-unit operators from shift coverage and raises roles to the work the workflows record. Unit and role headcounts are tier C estimates.

Facility counts and capacities are as at the end of 2021. In 2019-2020 the thermal units still burned coal from the company's own mine; the process map keeps coal mining and conversions as processes because they ran during the reference period.

Loaded cost per hour = wage x 1.40 (benefits about 25 percent, overhead about 15 percent). Power engineer wages come from the 2023 Alberta Wage and Salary Survey (src7), deflated by about 8 percent to 2021 and raised for shift premiums and overtime at large generators. Other wages are tier C estimates from Alberta pay levels in 2019-2022.
Occupation codes are NOC 2021 codes where the author was confident; others are null.

AESO rule details (offer deadlines, restatement rules, outage reporting under ISO rule 306.5) are described from general knowledge because the AESO rule documents opened as unreadable PDFs; the processes that depend on them are tier B or C accordingly.
Partner-operated units (the 50 percent Sheerness share) are offered and hedged by the marketing division but operated by the partner, so no plant staff are listed for them.
Volumes (work orders, trades, dispatches, invoices, faults) are tier C estimates scaled from fleet size; they are the numbers most worth checking against an operator's own data.
